sources.title: Connect MCP servers

sources.title: Multi-agent sandbox and tools

sources.title: gogcli docs: MCP server
sources.supports: gog ships its own typed stdio MCP server (`gog mcp`); by default it registers read tools only (Gmail search, get message, get thread) and hides every write tool.

sources.title: gogcli command reference: gog auth add
sources.supports: The authorization command takes a Gmail scope mode of full, readonly, send or read-send, and its --readonly flag requests read-only OAuth scopes.

corrections: The 9 Oct verifier note says gogcli has no read-only-only Gmail scope. The upstream command reference lists `--gmail-scope full|readonly|send|read-send` and says `--readonly` on `gog auth add` requests read-only OAuth scopes, so a read-only grant can be requested; the catalog's hedge 'if the installed version supports it' can be firmed up, pending a check on the installed binary.

The 9 Oct text treats the `

-gmail` wrapper as new code. Upstream gogcli ships a stdio MCP server (`gog mcp`) that exposes only read tools unless `--allow-write` is passed, so the config entry can run gog directly with an `--allow-tool` list and no wrapper.

The 9 Oct needs list stops at the per-agent allow list. With sandbox mode 'all' (Happy's setting) the installed docs add a second gate: MCP tools are filtered out unless `tools.sandbox.tools` also names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:101 and :130).
unverified: gog is not installed on this Mac; the flags come from the upstream main-branch docs and must be confirmed with `gog mcp --list-tools` and `gog auth add --help` on the version Homebrew installs.

Whether both adults' tokens would sit in one keyring under the happy user: upstream says tokens use the platform keyring by default with a file backend for headless hosts; splitting them with a per-adult GOG_HOME is my inference from the paths doc.
Refresh-token lifetime for a self-made Google OAuth client left in testing status was not checked in this run; Google's scope page does mark gmail.readonly as a Restricted scope.
The promptfoo injection canary is an in-house test, not an OpenClaw feature.

one_line: Happy writes drafts into the owner's own Gmail Drafts folder; the owner reviews and sends from Gmail, and Happy has no way to send.
how_short: `gog --gmail-no-send mcp --allow-write --allow-tool gmail_create_draft,gmail_update_draft`; fail-closed `before_tool_call` block on any send tool; CLI drafts thread with `--reply-to-message-id`.

sources.title: gogcli docs: MCP server
sources.supports: In gog's MCP mode the draft tools appear only with the write flag, the send tools need a separate send flag on top, and the no-send policy blocks sending while drafts still work.

sources.title: gogcli command reference: gog gmail drafts create
sources.supports: The draft-create command accepts a reply-to message id (and a thread id), which sets the reply headers and thread so the draft lands inside the conversation.

sources.title: Gmail API: Choose scopes
sources.supports: Google offers no drafts-only scope: the compose scope covers managing drafts and sending, and modify also includes sending, so the token itself can always send.

sources.title: Tool call policy hooks
sources.supports: A plugin's before_tool_call handler that returns a block is terminal, so a send tool can be denied in code the model cannot argue with.

corrections: The catalog says 'verify `--reply-to-message-id` on drafts create, else drafts are unthreaded'. The upstream command reference documents `--reply-to-message-id` and `--thread-id` on `gog gmail drafts create`, plus a separate `gog gmail drafts reply <messageId>`; the installed SKILL.md (line 59) merely omits them.

The catalog describes a custom MCP around `gog gmail drafts create` with the hook as the only send barrier. Upstream gog's own MCP server already keeps `gmail_send_message` and `gmail_send_draft` behind a separate `--allow-gmail-send` flag, so the hook is a second layer, not the only one.
unverified: Whether gog's MCP tool `gmail_create_draft` exposes the reply and thread parameters that the CLI command has; if not, threaded drafts need a thin wrapper over the CLI.
gog is not installed here; confirm the tool names with `gog mcp --allow-write --list-tools` after install.
The promptfoo 'send attempt is blocked' test is in-house.
